- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for next forecast.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to counter mean reversion.
- Model exhibits strong lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns bullish after 3–5 days, forecast should adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price peaks; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast mean, especially when sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; apply smoothing filter to forecast to reduce volatility.
